title: Prayer Journal Examples: 10 Real Sample Entries
description: Prayer journal examples to copy: 10 sample entries using ACTS, SOAP, letters to God, prayer lists and answered prayers, plus a free page to write your own.
h1: Prayer journal examples: 10 sample entries to learn from
intro: A prayer journal entry is usually a short, dated prayer written to God. Most include a Bible verse, thanks, a few requests and space for answers. Below are 10 prayer journal entry examples in different styles, so you can see what each one looks like and pick the one that fits you.

writer.title: Dear Lord,
writer.hint: Pick a style from the examples below and write your own entry here.

sections.h2: What a prayer journal entry looks like

blocks.p: There is no one right way. A good entry is honest, specific and dated. It can be three lines or three pages. Most entries have some of these parts:

ul: **The date,** so you can look back later.
**A verse or passage** you read before praying.
**Praise and thanks,** naming who God is and what He has done.
**Confession,** if something is between you and God.
**Requests** for yourself and others, with names and real needs.

blocks.p: The examples below use made up details, but the style of each is real. Copy any style you like. If you want boxes to fill in, use the [prayer journal template](/prayer-journal-template/).

sections.h2: Prayer journal entry examples by method

blocks.p: ACTS stands for Adoration, Confession, Thanksgiving and Supplication. It keeps your prayer balanced. Learn more on the [ACTS prayer journal](/prayer-journal-acts/) page.

example.label: ACTS
example.title: Father,
example.text:
A: You are patient and You never give up on me.
C: I was short with my coworker today. I am sorry.
T: Thank You for the rain, for my health, for Sunday dinner.
S: Please give Mark wisdom with his new job.
Help me have a kind word ready tomorrow.

blocks.p: SOAP stands for Scripture, Observation, Application and Prayer. It starts in the Bible and ends in prayer.

example.label: SOAP
example.title: Matthew 6:34
example.text:
S: Jesus tells me not to worry about tomorrow.
O: Jesus knows I tend to borrow trouble from next week.
A: Today I will only plan today and leave the rest.
P: Lord, take my worry about the bills.
Teach me to trust You one day at a time.

blocks.p: For busy days. Thank You, sorry, please.

example.label: Three lines
example.title: Lord,
example.text:
Thank You for getting the kids to school on time.
I am sorry for complaining all morning.
Please help me rest tonight.

sections.h2: Examples of written prayers for different seasons

blocks.h3: 4. A letter to God on a hard day

example.label: Letter
example.title: Dear God,
example.text:
I do not have nice words today. I am just tired.
The doctor called and I am scared.
I know You are near the brokenhearted.
Please stay close to me tonight.
I will trust You even when I cannot see how.
Love, me.

example.label: Gratitude
example.title: Thank You, Lord,

example.label: Guidance
example.title: Father,
example.text:
I have two job offers and I do not know which to take.
One pays more. One is closer to home.
Show me what matters most to You.
Close the wrong door and open the right one.
I want Your plan more than my own.

sections.h2: Prayer list and answered prayer examples

blocks.h3: 7. A prayer list by day of the week

head: Day
Who I pray for
Example request
rows: Peace at home, Dad's back pain
Missionaries, a country in the news
Patience, rest, time in the Word

example.label: Answered prayers
example.title: What I asked, what God did
example.text:
Jan 4: Grandma's surgery to go well. Answered Jan 9, home and healing.
Feb 2: A car we can afford. Answered Feb 20, from a friend at church.
Mar 1: Peace with my brother. Still waiting. Keep praying.

blocks.p: Notice the dates. They turn a list into a record of God's faithfulness. Read more [prayer journal ideas](/prayer-journal-ideas/) for other ways to track answers.

sections.h2: Prayer journal examples for other people

example.label: For my husband
example.title: Lord,
example.text:
Be with Dave at work this week. Give him a clear mind.
Protect his health and his heart.
Help him lead our home with love and patience.
Help me support him and not nag.
Grow our friendship again.

blocks.p: See the full [prayer journal for your husband](/prayer-journal-for-husband/) for prompts by area of life.

example.label: For my daughter
example.title: Father,
example.text:
Thank You for Lily and her big laugh.
Give her a good friend at her new school.
Help her know she is loved by You.
Keep her safe on the bus and at play.
Give me patience at bedtime.

blocks.p: For more, see the [prayer journal for your children](/prayer-journal-for-your-children/).

ul: **Writing only requests.** Lists of needs are fine, but add praise and thanks so prayer is not just a wish list.
**Being too vague.** Bless my family is a good start. Help my son make one good friend at school is easier to pray and to see answered.
**Skipping the date.** Without dates you cannot see how long you waited or how God answered over time.
**Trying to sound holy.** God wants your real voice. Plain words are better than words you would never say out loud.
**Giving up after a missed week.** Just start again with today's date. No catch up needed.

sections.h2: How to write your own entry

steps.name: Pick a style
steps.text: Choose one of the examples above. ACTS or the three line prayer are easy to start with.

steps.name: Read a short passage
steps.text: A psalm or a few verses. Write the reference at the top.

steps.name: Write to God in your own words
steps.text: Short sentences are fine. Use names and real details.

steps.name: Date it
steps.text: So you can see later when you prayed and when He answered.

steps.name: Come back and add answers
steps.text: Mark answered prayers in the margin or on an answered prayers page.

blocks.tip: Stuck on what to say? Our [prayer journal prompts](/prayer-journal-prompts/) give you over 100 starting points. Prefer a guided format on your phone? The [Prayer Journal for Women](/prayer-journal-for-women/) Android app, coming soon on Google Play, walks you through a verse, reflection and prayer every week.

faq.q: What is an example of a prayer journal entry?
faq.a: A simple example: the date, a verse such as Psalm 46:1, a line of thanks, a line of confession, and a request for someone by name. For instance, thank You for a good night's sleep, forgive me for being impatient, and please give my mom strength for her treatment this week. Later you add how God answered.

faq.q: How long should a prayer journal entry be?
faq.a: As long as you need. Many entries are three to ten lines. On hard days you may write a full page, and on busy days a single sentence. Short and regular is usually better than long and rare.

faq.q: Should I write my prayers to God directly?
faq.a: Many people find it helps. Writing to God, starting with Dear Lord or Father, turns your journal into real prayer instead of notes about prayer. It also keeps your words honest because you are speaking to Someone who already knows your heart.

faq.q: What is the difference between a prayer journal and a Bible journal?
faq.a: A prayer journal focuses on talking to God: praise, confession, thanks and requests. A Bible journal focuses on what you learn from Scripture. Many people combine them by reading first, then praying about what they read. See our [Bible journal](/bible-journal/) page for more.

faq.q: Can I share my prayer journal entries?
faq.a: You can, but you do not have to. Prayer journals are usually private so you can be completely honest. Some parents later share prayer pages with grown children as a gift. Entries you write on this site stay on your device unless you print them.
